clue.text: Fortification as a help to royal residents, roughly speaking?

indicators.note: said loosely, so the phrase is pronounced approximately rather than exactly

parts.note: an assistant to those living in a royal residence is a palace aide

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a defensive wall counts as assistance to the people living in a royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly speaking' says the sound is only approximate: PALACE AIDE, said quickly, comes close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence of pointed stakes set in the ground is a classic defensive barrier.

clue.text: Physicist laying down principle involving speed of light

indicators.note: one word wraps around another, so the principle takes in the symbol for light speed

parts.note: a plank is one principle of a political party's platform
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A scientist sets out a fundamental rule that involves how fast light travels.
explanation.walkthrough: A PLANK is a policy in a party platform, the thing a politician lays down; C, the physicist's symbol for light speed, goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Planck was the German scientist who founded quantum theory.

clue.text: Many soldiers using manacle around limb — it's not right

indicators.note: says the following letter should be absent, so the abbreviation for right is struck out

parts.note: a leg iron is a shackle fastened round a leg

explanation.surface: A large military force is restrained with shackles on their limbs, which seems unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's not right' removes R from LEG IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion was a unit of several thousand troops, and the word also means a great multitude.

clue.text: In this a single person may lay heart open

definitions.text: In this a single person may lay heart open

parts.words: In this a single person may lay heart open
parts.note: sounds like a lonely confession, but describes a card game for one in which the player lays cards from the heart suit face up

explanation.surface: A lonely person might pour out their feelings in this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay heart open' suggests emotional honesty; it is really laying out a card of hearts face up in a game played alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience, the card game played by one player alone, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Repeat instruction from attorney to limit resettling of alien

parts.note: DA stands for district attorney, the American public prosecutor
a cap is an upper limit, as on spending

indicators.note: the letters are moved and settled again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer advises restricting where a foreigner may relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resettling' rearranges OF ALIEN into OALFINE. 'to' only joins the pieces. The musical direction tells the player to go back to the start and stop at the word 'fine'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical marking tells a performer to go back to the beginning and play through to the marked ending.

clue.text: Official survey succeeded penetrating extremists in college students

indicators.note: the outermost letters of the following word are taken
one piece pushes into the middle of another

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A government poll found that a successor had infiltrated radicals within a college's student body.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS, the National Union of Students, is a UK convention; 'penetrating' places S after the N, splitting the student body.
explanation.definitionFit: A national count of the population carried out by the government is an official survey.

clue.text: Uplift provided by drug after normal office hours?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
work done late is done after the usual working day

explanation.surface: A drug taken in the evening once the office has closed gives a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift someone is to raise their spirits and make them joyful.

clue.text: Onset of snoring — companion sleeps having imbibed soft drink

indicators.note: the start of the next word, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: one word swallows another, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: naps are short sleeps
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Someone starts snoring as their partner dozes off after downing a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award; p means soft (piano) in music. The 'soft drink' is a trap: the answer is a strong spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong spirit distilled from grain or fruit, originally from Germany and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Pass judgement on grammatical structure

definitions.meaning: a judge decides the punishment for a convicted person
a complete unit of words with subject and verb

explanation.definitionFit: A judge pronounces punishment on a criminal, and a grammarian studies a complete written statement with a main verb.

clue.text: Herb going out with a nice gal

indicators.note: the letters leave their places and reform, as if going out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Herb is a man who is dating a pleasant young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name in a dating story; it is the plant. 'going out' rearranges A NICE GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall aromatic plant whose candied stems are used to decorate cakes.

clue.text: A guerrilla fighter invades an old capital city

indicators.note: one piece enters the territory of the other

parts.note: taken as written
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel soldier attacks a former seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: This German city was Charlemagne's seat of power and the base of his empire.

clue.text: Upset Latin masters?

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teachers of a classical language might be annoyed by this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges LATIN MASTERS, and the whole clue describes what would annoy such teachers: a poor rendering of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering a passage into another language wrongly is exactly what would vex teachers of Latin.

clue.text: Bash about someone who needs to be taught manners

parts.note: c is circa, Latin for about

parts.words: someone who needs to be taught manners
parts.note: a lout is a rude, uncouth person

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a rude person deserves a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash someone is to hit them hard, a sharp blow.

clue.text: Simple book caused worry: it's the least borrowers can expect

definitions.text: it's the least borrowers can expect

parts.note: a primer is a basic first reading book
ate as in 'what's eating you?', meaning troubled

explanation.surface: A children's reader caused anxiety, which is the minimum a borrower can expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ate' in the sense of 'what's eating you?': troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest lending rate a bank offers is given to its most creditworthy customers.

clue.text: Having resorted to spin, charm, I admitted disliking folk

indicators.note: let in, so one letter is placed inside the rest
sorted again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turned to propaganda and flattery, confessing a dislike of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' looks like part of 'resorted to', meaning turned to, but it is the anagram signal and 'to' belongs to the fodder; 'admitted' lets I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hates mankind and avoids society is unsociable by nature.

clue.text: Reading only? All three rs — let's not have a cutback!

parts.note: of the three Rs, only Reading, giving its letter R

indicators.note: says a letter should be left out

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, stand for basic schooling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher protests at a plan to cut back schooling to reading alone, losing the other basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The three Rs' (reading, writing and arithmetic) is a British phrase for basic schooling. 'let's not have a' removes A from EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a cut or lowering in amount, such as a cut in spending.

clue.text: Manages to support those people who could inspire others?

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece underneath holds up the one above

parts.note: them refers to other people
uses as in makes use of, manages with

explanation.surface: Others make do with backing a particular group who might motivate others.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to support' puts USES under THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine goddesses of Greek myth were believed to give poets and artists their creative inspiration.

clue.text: Plant with sign of new life ideal for transplanting

parts.note: a bud is the first growth of a plant in spring

indicators.note: moving to another place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener sees new spring growth on a plant that is just right for moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for transplanting' rearranges IDEAL into DLEIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub, often called the butterfly bush, that attracts butterflies.

clue.text: Dodgy building in which there may be several clubs

definitions.meaning: a shaky structure liable to fall

definitions.text: in which there may be several clubs
definitions.meaning: a structure made of playing cards would include cards of the clubs suit

explanation.definitionFit: A tower of playing cards is a flimsy structure, and it would include cards of the suit of clubs.

clue.text: Comrade's resistance stopping monster

definitions.note: read as 'Comrade is', so the definition is just comrade

indicators.note: a letter blocks a gap in the middle of a word, as a stopper plugs a hole

parts.note: a fiend is a demon or monster
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A fellow soldier fights back against a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Comrade's' as 'Comrade is'. R goes inside FIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or ally, a close pal.

clue.text: Find me in Jerusalem as one seeking early departure

indicators.note: one word goes inside another

parts.note: Sion (Zion) is a name for Jerusalem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilgrim is invited to meet someone in Jerusalem who wants to leave soon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Luke's Gospel, the old man in the Temple at Jerusalem asks to 'depart in peace' after seeing the infant Jesus, the Nunc Dimittis.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the aged man who held the infant Jesus prayed that he could now die in peace.

clue.text: Endemic is out of control — get these?

definitions.text: Endemic is out of control — get these?

indicators.note: running wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disease is spreading unchecked, so you had better obtain treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' rearranges ENDEMIC IS, and the whole clue says what you would want when disease spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs and remedies are what sufferers need when an illness spreads out of control.

clue.text: Suppress utterance of European

indicators.note: the following word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Someone is told to silence what a European person says.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to restrain or curb it.

clue.text: Bones in fish beginning to irritate

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Fish bones start to annoy someone eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' also means to complain, which fits 'irritate', but here it is just the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpal bones form the wrist, the plural of carpus.

clue.text: The woman getting married proved to be very old-fashioned

parts.note: she refers to a woman
wed means married

explanation.surface: A bride's wedding turned out to be extremely traditional.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic spelling of 'showed' is what 'very old-fashioned' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic spelling of showed, meaning demonstrated.

clue.text: Island's policy needs external support

indicators.note: says the support must go round the outside of the policy

parts.note: a base is a support or foundation
a line is an official policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: An island nation's strategy requires help from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'external' tells which way round the container goes: the support sits outside the policy. 'needs' is part of that signal, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Bali, the Indonesian island, or to its people and culture.

clue.text: Son has need of trousers

parts.note: lacks means does not have, so needs

explanation.surface: A boy requires a pair of trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual trousers, not part of a suit.

clue.text: Poor academic is said to be intimidated

indicators.note: spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: lean means poor or meagre, and a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A badly paid university lecturer is rumoured to have been bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is an Oxford or Cambridge lecturer; LEAN DON, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being leaned on means being pressured or bullied into something.
